services.intro: Our licensed plumbers work on homes across Lincolnwood, from the village’s older post-war blocks to newer builds.

cards.paragraph: [Lincolnwood’s Stormwater Master Plan found the village sewer system handles only a 2- to 3-year level of protection](https://www.lincolnwoodil.org/Archive.aspx?ADID=945), short of the 10-year standard the village is working toward. Older clay lines under its post-war streets add to the risk, cracking or filling with roots. That combination means a hard rain can push a weak line past its limit fast. We camera-inspect your line, clear what’s blocking it, and talk through whether a backflow valve makes sense.

Lincolnwood is a tight, built-out village bordered by Chicago, Skokie and Niles, and it sees the same hard summer storms that soak the rest of the north suburbs. An older line can only take so much rain before it backs up, and when that happens inside your home, waiting even an hour makes the cleanup bigger. Day or night, including weekends and holidays, our line stays open, and we work to get a plumber to your door as soon as we can.

[More than two-thirds of Lincolnwood homes were built before 1970, median year 1958](https://cmap.illinois.gov/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Lincolnwood.pdf), so most still run on original clay or cast iron drain lines. Cast iron scales up inside over the decades, and clay joints let tree roots work in, so a quick clear often doesn’t last. That usually shows up as the same kitchen or basement drain backing up again. We clear the line and run a camera through it first.

[Lincolnwood switched its water supply from Chicago to Evanston’s Lake Michigan system in 2020](https://dailynorthwestern.com/2020/09/23/city/lincolnwood-completes-construction-project-connecting-to-evanston-water-supply), after years of steep Chicago rate increases. The new supply is still treated lake water, so the same minerals that build up inside any tank over the years are still at work. A heater installed before the switch has run through two different supplies. If yours rumbles or runs out of hot water early, it’s worth a look. We help you repair it or size a replacement.

Toilets and fixtures in Lincolnwood’s older homes have usually been swapped out at least once, but the supply valves and seals behind them don’t always get replaced at the same time. That mismatch is often why a toilet runs constantly or a shower valve starts leaking years after a remodel. Left alone, a running toilet adds up on the water bill, and a hidden leak can damage the subfloor. From a quick valve repair to a full fixture swap, we handle the job, old or new.

Many Lincolnwood homes still carry original supply lines behind plaster walls, and decades-old pipe corrodes from the inside where you can’t see it. A slow leak can run for weeks before a stain or soft spot in the floor gives it away, and by then it may have reached the framing underneath. If you notice a drop in pressure or a damp spot, it’s worth tracing down. We find the leak, repair or replace the pipe, and check nearby sections.

cards.paragraph: With [Lincolnwood’s sewer system rated for only a 2- to 3-year level of protection](https://www.lincolnwoodil.org/Archive.aspx?ADID=945), a sump pump is often the last line of defense between a hard rain and a wet basement. A pump that’s undersized, old or without a battery backup can fail right when a storm knocks out power, which is exactly when you need it most. A failed pump usually means standing water within hours. We test, repair and replace sump pumps, and can add a battery backup for when the power drops.

faq.q: Do you have plumbers near me in Lincolnwood?
faq.a: Yes. Our plumbers work all over Lincolnwood and the nearby north suburban towns, including Morton Grove, Niles and Skokie. Call us 24/7 and we’ll get a plumber to you.

faq.q: Are you licensed and bonded in Illinois?
faq.a: Yes. We’re licensed and bonded in Illinois, and we’ve been serving Chicagoland homeowners since 1993.

faq.q: How much does a plumber cost in Lincolnwood?
faq.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.

faq.q: Why do I keep getting the same drain clog?
faq.a: [More than two-thirds of Lincolnwood homes were built before 1970](https://cmap.illinois.gov/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Lincolnwood.pdf), and most still run on their original clay or cast iron drain lines. Roots or scale inside them cause the same spot to clog again and again. Clearing the clog only buys time. We run a camera through the line so you know whether the pipe itself needs repair.

faq.q: Why does my basement flood during a heavy storm?
faq.a: [Lincolnwood’s sewer system is currently rated for only a 2- to 3-year level of protection](https://www.lincolnwoodil.org/Archive.aspx?ADID=945), and the village is working through a ten-project plan to bring it up to a 10-year standard. Until those projects are finished, a hard storm can still push water back into a basement. We check your line and can recommend a backflow valve or sump pump backup.
